knowledge_point.title: Using the Double-Angle Formula to Simplify Products

question.:question/worked-solution:
Put $x=\frac{4\pi}{9}$. Recall $2\sin x\cos x=\sin(2x)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{4\sin x\cos x}{\cos(2x)} &=2\frac{2\sin x\cos x}{\cos(2x)} \\ &=2\frac{\sin(2x)}{\cos(2x)} \\ &=2\tan(2x)
\end{aligned}
$$

The denominator is nonzero, and $\tan(2x)=\sin(2x)/\cos(2x)$.

Substitute $x=\frac{4\pi}{9}$ and double the whole angle: $2x=\frac{8\pi}{9}$. The result is

$$
2\tan\left(\frac{8\pi}{9}\right) .
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Put $x=\frac{\pi}{9}$. Expand the square and combine the squared terms.

$$
\begin{aligned}
(\sin x+\cos x)^2 &=\sin^2 x+2\sin x\cos x+\cos^2 x \\ &=1+2\sin x\cos x \\ &=1+\sin(2x)
\end{aligned}
$$

Here $\sin^2 x+\cos^2 x=1$ and $2\sin x\cos x=\sin(2x)$.

Substitute $x=\frac{\pi}{9}$ and double the whole angle: $2x=\frac{2\pi}{9}$. The result is

$$
1+\sin\left(\frac{2\pi}{9}\right) .
$$

knowledge_point.title: Using the Double-Angle Formula to Simplify Products

question.:question/worked-solution:
Put $x=\frac{4\pi}{9}$. Recall $2\sin x\cos x=\sin(2x)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{2\sin x\cos x}{\cos(2x)} &=\frac{2\sin x\cos x}{\cos(2x)} \\ &=\frac{\sin(2x)}{\cos(2x)} \\ &=\tan(2x)
\end{aligned}
$$

The denominator is nonzero, and $\tan(2x)=\sin(2x)/\cos(2x)$.

Substitute $x=\frac{4\pi}{9}$ and double the whole angle: $2x=\frac{8\pi}{9}$. The result is

$$
\tan\left(\frac{8\pi}{9}\right) .
$$
